Program Description

The BA (Hons) Criminology is an undergraduate degree designed to allow students to delve into the fascinating and diverse world of criminology, exploring areas such as drugs, cybercrime and terrorism. With this course students will be able to develop an understanding of contemporary criminology concepts and theories, looking at how they are viewed from a variety of perspectives. If students have aspirations of working in the criminal justice sector and want to build a strong overview of criminology and its effects within modern society, then this course is an excellent place to start.

Designed by practising criminologists, this three year degree programme will allow students to look at areas such as drugs, cybercrime, migration, mass incarceration, terrorism, and trafficking in detail. Students will get to consider how these areas are viewed by groups from various backgrounds and with different outlooks, including how gender, race and cultural perspectives and issues can impact opinion.

This course is particularly interesting if students are looking to work in the criminal justice sector or associated fields. Students will benefit from learning in various ways, giving them a well-rounded understanding of both the theory and practice of criminology. This will enable students to develop a comprehensive understanding of criminology and apply this to current socio-economic policies and conditions.

Students will learn through a variety of group sessions, workshops, digital media and a wide range of learning resources, completing a research methods module and a dissertation or research project in the final year. In addition to their knowledge of criminology, students will gain a wide range of analytical, research, problem solving and communication skills, which are in high demand by employers.

Program Description

This BA (Hons) Criminology and Policing degree combines ULaw's expertise in contemporary criminology and professional policing to give students a comprehensive understanding of criminological theories that students will be able to apply to current socio-economic policies and conditions. Students will develop an understanding of criminology from different perspectives in areas such as crime, criminality, victims and vulnerability.

ULaw's Criminology and Policing degree will prepare students for a career within the criminal justice system in roles such as policing, research or youth work. On this course, students will benefit from a theoretical basis as well as a vocational application of the course content, preparing students for a career in the criminal justice sector, police service or associated fields.

This three year degree allows students to combine criminology study with policing modules which cover aspects of the national policing curriculum. Students will look at areas such as drugs, cybercrime, migration, terrorism, and trafficking in detail. Students will consider how these areas are viewed by groups from various backgrounds, including how gender, race and cultural perspectives can impact opinion.

Students will be taught by experts in criminology who have worked directly with government departments, as well as former police officers for a practical, hands-on education. This course sets students up for a career in the criminal justice sector, the police service or the NGO and charity sector, among others.

Please note that this BA Criminology and Policing programme does not qualify as a pre-join degree to enable direct entry into a police service. Students wishing to pursue a career as a police officer on graduation would need to enter a service via the degree holder entry route.

Program Description

The law degree, known as an LLB or Bachelor of Laws, is equivalent to a BA or BSc. This degree is perfect for students whose career aspiration is to be a solicitor or barrister in the UK as it will mean students are prepared in part for the new Solicitors Qualifying Examination (SQE1) or to progress onto the Bar Practice Course (if they wish to qualify as a barrister). And if students have set their sights on a career in politics, business or journalism, the transferable skills they will learn on the law degree will give them an excellent launch pad for these ambitions and more. With a professionally focused qualification, students can expect to learn practical skills coupled with a focus on their future employability.

The LLB law course will also offer students the flexibility to specialise more and more as they progress to focus on what interests them, with opportunities to study anything from Business Law to International Law.

Students can expect something different to the traditional three year Bachelor of Laws degree when they study the LLB. Over 90% of the University of Law's tutors are qualified solicitors, barristers and judges so students will learn to apply law and learn the most relevant and practical skills that employers are looking for. The University of Law has designed the LLB to be the first truly professional undergraduate law degree.

Studying law is the start to a wide, varied and exciting legal career. It offers more diversity than almost any other profession, whether students want to be a company secretary, a solicitor, a paralegal or a high court judge. It is also one of the best qualifications for going on to succeed in other careers. Students can find University of Law graduates working in politics, journalism, business, HR and finance and more all over the world.

Program Description

The Accelerated LLB is a Qualifying Law Degree that covers all the same material as the LLB undergraduate law degree, but in two years rather than three. It is designed for those who are able to dedicate extra time to their studies on a weekly basis. Still packed with great transferrable skills training, students can feel confident that they will graduate ready to take on the challenges of any career path they might wish to follow. If students are eager to qualify as a solicitor or barrister then this course will help them jump-start their legal career. Students can complete their Qualifying Law Degree in just two years with the Accelerated LLB, allowing them to move on to postgraduate study sooner. Studying this degree will also mean students are prepared in part for the new Solicitors Qualifying Examination (SQE 1) or to progress onto the Bar Practice Course (if they wish to qualify as a barrister).

With the Accelerated LLB law course, students will graduate with the knowledge and solid intellectual skills to pursue a career in a wide variety of legal professions. University of Law law graduates choose to use their law degree as a passport for entry into a wide range of careers, including business, media, finance and banking, criminology, governmental bodies and departments, and the police force.

The two year Accelerated Law degree is designed to get students to the next stage of their professional training as a lawyer or start their career as quickly as possible, without compromising on quality. The University of Law focuses on teaching students the most relevant and practical skills that employers are looking for.

The Accelerated LLB is a faster, more intensive route taught by the same tutors and using the same high-quality teaching methods as the three year law degree. Over 90% of the University of Law tutors are qualified lawyers so students will learn to apply law in realistic and genuinely applicable ways.

Program Description

The LLB (Hons) Law with Business is a three year full-time degree. It will give students a wide understanding of key legal topics and related skills, as well as developing business skills and competencies. As well as enabling students to progress to the next stage of legal training as a solicitor or barrister, it’s also a great choice if students want to move into a career outside of the legal sector as they will study a range of business modules that will make them employment-ready. Studying this degree will also mean students are prepared in part for the new Solicitors Qualifying Examination (SQE 1) or to progress onto the Bar Practice Course (if they wish to qualify as a barrister).

With the LLB Law with Business degree, students will gain valuable real-world skills and experience through their study and business-related work placements. Mock trials, law simulations and pro bono work will ensure students graduate with a practical understanding of law and business. Students will learn valuable transferable skills that could help in various professional careers, such as in the finance, banking and legal sectors.

The Law with Business three year full-time degree will give students a wide understanding of key legal topics and related skills. It also allows students to develop business skills and competencies. The University of Law teaches students practical skills that are relevant and applicable to the realities of working in the legal or wider business sectors. Over 90% of the University of Law tutors are qualified lawyers, so students will learn how to apply law from experienced professionals in practical methods that have been tried and tested in the real world.

With the addition of a variety of business related modules, students can customise their learning to suit their career interests. Whether they are interested in marketing, finance or HR, or many other areas, students can explore many exciting business fields in tandem with their legal studies. The business modules will give students a great insight into how different departments within companies operate and perform together to keep a business working efficiently.

Program Description

The LLB (Hons) Law with Criminology is a three year degree that combines legal studies with an exploration of different aspects of criminology, including crime, criminal justice and criminal behaviour. With specific modules focusing on criminology, students' studies will not only give them a great legal qualification, but they will also open up fascinating career avenues within the criminological world too. Studying this degree will also mean students are prepared in part for the new Solicitors Qualifying Examination (SQE 1) or to progress onto the Bar Practice Course (if they wish to qualify as a barrister).

With the LLB Law and Criminology qualification, students will also explore social responses to crime and criminality, and look at the processes and consequences of law-making, law-breaking and law enforcement.

The skills and knowledge students will gain on this Law with Criminology course will not only set them up for a career in the legal field but prepare them for other exciting options. For instance, establishments in government, education, and many more, find a law degree highly desirable – so students will have plenty of career choices after graduation.

This course focuses on key legal topics and a variety of different aspects of criminology, including crime, criminal justice and criminal behaviour. It’s an ideal choice if students are looking to pursue a career in the legal sector or, more specifically, within the criminal justice system. In addition to studying key legal topics, students will also study Criminology modules which examine the nature of crime and how it operates. The course focuses on key concepts, such as the definition of crime and how it is perceived within society.

Studying this balanced combination of law and criminology means that students have a great choice of career options to choose from. Not only could students continue their studies to become a qualified lawyer, but they can consider careers in politics, journalism, business or criminal investigation and analysis. This course is a great starting point from which to launch a career in the exciting worlds of law and criminology.

Program Description

The LLB (Hons) Law with International Business combines legal studies with an exploration of different aspects of international business. This course is ideal for those looking to develop an understanding of modern global business practices that will complement a law degree. With key business modules that focus on marketing, HR and strategy on an international scale, students will get plenty of experience and knowledge in how international businesses operate successfully. Studying this degree will also mean students are prepared in part for the new Solicitors Qualifying Examination (SQE 1) or to progress onto the Bar Practice Course (if they wish to qualify as a barrister).

Through studying the LLB Law with International Business degree, students will develop knowledge of business and law in an international context, and gain the attributes to contribute to the global business strategy of organisations and resolve international business problems.

This course focuses on key legal topics and a variety of different aspects of international business practices. These include Human Resource Management, Marketing, Leadership and Strategic Management. It is designed to give students a well-balanced choice of subjects. Students will study all of the required areas of law to receive a Qualifying Law Degree as well as having a diverse range of international business modules.

Over 90% of the tutors are qualified lawyers so they will learn to apply law and develop the practical skills employers are looking for today. To make sure that students have the skills to be versatile, the University of Law has also embedded important transferable skills in their courses. The University of Law wants to make sure students feel confident that they can graduate and head straight into the workplace with the skills that employers are looking for.

With this course, students have the opportunity to choose to undertake a business research module in the third year. This double module offers students the chance to focus specifically on an aspect of international business that is of personal interest, allowing private research and study with the support and guidance of an allocated tutor.

Program Description

The LLB (Hons) Law Senior Status is a specifically designed degree for students who already hold an undergraduate degree and want to convert to law study over a two year period. Students can study all the necessary modules for a law degree while enjoying the flexibility of being able to select three LLB course options to suit areas that interest them. Studying this degree will also mean students are prepared in part for the new Solicitors Qualifying Examination (SQE 1) or to progress onto the Bar Practice Course (if they wish to qualify as a barrister).

During the LLB Senior Status degree, Students will develop excellent research and analytical skills and learn to present their ideas effectively both verbally and in writing. The course provides students with a wide range of analytical and transferable skills and is suitable for any profession requiring a non-specialised degree.

The LLB (Hons) Senior Status degree is a two year LLB programme specifically designed for students who already hold a degree. In addition to gaining a Qualifying Law Degree in just two years, the programme offers students the additional flexibility of being able to select three LLB course options in their second year.

This degree is taught by the same experienced, professional tutors as the standard three year LLB , using the same high-quality teaching methods. The course combines academic rigour with practical legal skills, providing students with the essential groundwork of their legal education while they study with other students in a professional business-like environment.

The Senior Status degree is a particularly good choice for overseas students because they may benefit from some exemptions in their home jurisdiction – a good example of this is the Canadian Law modules available as electives in the second year.

Program Description

The new MA Law (SQE1) is a law conversion course and includes the SQE1 Preparation Course, which prepares students for the SQE1 assessments. The course is designed for non-law graduates who want to qualify as a solicitor and gain a legal qualification at Master’s level. As an internationally recognised qualification, a Law Master’s is a great addition to a portfolio. With a strong level of support from the start, as well as four weeks guaranteed Qualifying Work Experience (QWE) within the Legal Advice Clinics. This course is a great introduction to law if students hold an undergraduate degree in another discipline. Successful completion of the MA Law (SQE1) also qualifies students to progress on to study the SQE2 Preparation Course to become a solicitor.

The University of Law's MA Law (SQE1) is a conversion course designed for non-law graduates. On successful completion of this course, including the SQE1 assessments, students will gain an internationally recognized Master’s qualification.

Although there is no longer a formal requirement for qualification as a solicitor, this course will give learners the academic legal knowledge they need (as part of Functioning Legal Knowledge (FLK) for SQE1) and will encourage learners to think like a lawyer from the start.

This MA Law conversion course also develops the key professional skills and behaviours required by lawyers, alongside skills required to pass professional examinations for qualification as a solicitor. In all modules there is a focus on combining knowledge and understanding of core areas of law with the ability to analyze, evaluate and form critical judgements about the law. Study is centred on practical activities that enable students to learn by doing to help them thrive as a lawyer in a work environment.

Many employers value the combination of a non-law undergraduate area of expertise combined with the solid grounding in core legal principles and legal skills, provided by a law conversion course.

With an emphasis on leadership and management, the programme develops an integrated and critically informed understanding of organisations in a global context.

Students examine real-world case studies to explore changing business conditions and the effects of different leadership decisions. The curriculum combines core business management principles with a distinctive focus on the relationship between business and law. Specialist electives in areas such as technology, healthcare, and professional services enable students to develop cross-sector expertise.

Learning is centred on practical application, collaborative work, and detailed case analysis. Students use business tools through case studies, simulations, and interactive group activities, applying management frameworks to complex workplace challenges. Teaching is delivered online by experienced practitioners and academics, providing opportunities to collaborate with peers and explore real-world business scenarios.

A structured MBA Challenge Set develops high-demand managerial and leadership capabilities through a series of practical, connected modules. Students apply their learning to workplace situations and build the skills needed to address complex organisational and executive challenges.

Professional coaching supports students in developing a tailored Personal Development Plan and translating their career goals into practical steps. This support can help them prepare to change direction, advance in their current field, or pursue senior leadership opportunities.
